title_en: What orthostatic intolerance is and when it appears
title_ko: 기립불내성이란 무엇이며 언제 나타나는가
text_en: Orthostatic intolerance means the body cannot keep up blood pressure and blood flow to the brain while upright, so a person feels light-headed or may faint. It belongs to the return of gravity, on landing day or on the Mars surface, not to floating in weightlessness, where there is no standing load.
text_ko: 기립불내성은 서 있는 자세에서 혈압과 뇌로 가는 혈류가 유지되지 않아 머리가 아찔해지거나 실신할 수 있는 상태를 말한다. 무중력 상태에서는 서 있는 자세에 따르는 부담이 없으므로, 이 문제는 떠다니는 동안이 아니라 착륙 당일이나 화성 표면처럼 중력이 다시 작용할 때 나타난다.

sources.title: Hazard: Gravity Fields
Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
Evidence Report: Risk of Orthostatic Intolerance During Re-exposure to Gravity

do_not_claim: Do not describe dizziness while floating in weightlessness as orthostatic intolerance: it needs a gravity or acceleration load. In flight it has shown up only under an applied load such as lower-body negative-pressure sessions.

title_en: Why blood pressure can fall on standing after weightlessness
title_ko: 무중력 뒤에 일어서면 혈압이 떨어질 수 있는 이유
text_en: In weightlessness body fluid moves toward the head, and the body responds by carrying less circulating blood volume; the unloaded heart also pumps less blood per beat once upright. When gravity returns and blood pools in the legs, blood pressure can fall if the blood vessels do not tighten enough in response.
text_ko: 무중력에서는 체액이 머리 쪽으로 쏠리고, 몸은 이에 맞춰 순환하는 혈액의 양을 줄인다. 부담이 줄어든 심장도 일어섰을 때 한 번에 내보내는 혈액량이 적어진다. 그래서 중력이 돌아와 혈액이 다리 쪽으로 몰릴 때 혈관이 충분히 수축하지 못하면 혈압이 떨어질 수 있다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Orthostatic Intolerance During Re-exposure to Gravity
Evidence Report: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations Contributing to Adverse Mission Performance and Health Outcomes
Hazard: Gravity Fields
NASA/TM-20205008196: Artemis Sustained Translational Acceleration Limits

numbers: Plasma volume on return: 4.4% lower (Apollo), 8.4-15.9% lower (Skylab missions), 5-19% lower on landing day even after fluid loading; left-ventricular mass in bed rest fell 4.7%, 8.0% and 15.6% after 2, 6 and 12 weeks (NASA HRP Evidence Report on orthostatic intolerance, 2015). Going from sitting to standing lowers cardiac output by 10-20% in healthy people on Earth (NASA/TM-20205008196, 2020).
do_not_claim: Low blood volume alone does not decide who gets symptoms: everyone tested was low on volume at landing, yet only some became intolerant.

title_en: Whether Mars gravity protects is not known
title_ko: 화성 중력의 보호 효과는 알려져 있지 않다
text_en: Standing tolerance has never been measured in partial gravity, so it is unknown whether Mars gravity, about one-third of Earth's, protects against light-headedness on standing. The conservative planning assumption, made so far for the Moon, is that partial gravity does not protect. Fainting there could also have worse consequences, since no medical team is waiting on site.
text_ko: 부분 중력에서 서 있는 자세를 얼마나 견디는지는 측정된 적이 없어, 지구의 삼분의 일쯤인 화성 중력이 일어설 때의 아찔함을 막아 주는지는 알려져 있지 않다. 지금까지 달 임무를 대상으로 세운 보수적인 가정은 부분 중력이 이 문제를 막아 주지 않는다는 것이다. 또한 화성에는 지구에서처럼 곁에서 대기하는 의료진이 없으므로 실신했을 때의 결과가 더 나쁠 수 있다.

sources.title: NASA/TM-20205008196: Artemis Sustained Translational Acceleration Limits
Evidence Report: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations Contributing to Adverse Mission Performance and Health Outcomes
Evidence Report: Risk of Orthostatic Intolerance During Re-exposure to Gravity
Hazard: Gravity Fields

numbers: Mars gravity is about one-third of Earth's (NASA, Hazard: Gravity Fields) or 0.38 g, lunar gravity 0.16 g; after 14-16 days of bed rest all men but only half the women completed 10 minutes at a tilt equal to about half of Earth gravity (NASA/TM-20205008196, 2020).
do_not_claim: Do not say that lunar or Martian gravity protects, or that it does not: it is unknown and the 'no protection' position is a planning assumption. It has also not been shown whether fluid loading or compression garments are needed for descent to or ascent from Mars.

title_en: Preparing for the return of gravity
title_ko: 중력이 돌아오는 때에 대비하기
text_en: Preparation for the return of gravity combines regular exercise during the flight, drinking the prescribed fluid with salt before landing, and wearing a lower-body compression garment. Each measure helps, but none on its own fully prevents light-headedness on standing, so they are used together.
text_ko: 중력이 돌아오는 때에 대비해 비행 중에는 규칙적으로 운동하고, 착륙 전에는 처방받은 대로 수분과 염분을 보충하며, 하체 압박복을 착용한다. 각각 도움이 되지만 어느 하나만으로는 일어설 때의 아찔함을 완전히 막지 못하므로 함께 쓴다.

sources.title: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B: Water - Human Consumption
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations Contributing to Adverse Mission Performance and Health Outcomes

numbers: Station crews exercise 6-7 days a week for 1.5 hours a day (NASA, Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness, 2025). Fluid load before entry: at least 1 L per crew member, taken with salt (NASA OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B, 2023). Fluid retention peaks about 2-3 hours after drinking, so timing matters (NASA HRP Evidence Report on cardiovascular adaptations, 2022).
do_not_claim: Do not say that fluid loading, exercise or a compression garment each 'prevents' the problem. Do not advise adding salt routinely in flight: sodium is otherwise limited, and the salt belongs to the prescribed fluid load before landing.

title_en: First steps when light-headedness starts
title_ko: 머리가 아찔해지기 시작할 때 먼저 할 일
text_en: If light-headedness starts after landing or on the surface, sitting down, drinking more fluid and getting up more slowly are the usual first steps. Compression stockings or garments can also help keep blood pressure from dropping when upright.
text_ko: 착륙 후나 화성 표면에서 머리가 아찔해지기 시작하면 우선 앉고, 물을 더 마시고, 일어설 때는 천천히 일어나는 것이 좋다. 압박 스타킹이나 압박복도 서 있을 때 혈압이 떨어지는 것을 줄이는 데 도움이 될 수 있다.

sources.title: Low Blood Pressure
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

do_not_claim: General low-blood-pressure self-care from Earth guidance; not tested in returning crews. Do not suggest any medicine.

title_en: Tensing muscles to ease a faint feeling
title_ko: 실신할 것 같을 때 근육에 힘 주기
text_en: After gravity has returned, if a faint feeling comes on while upright, tensing the muscles of the legs, abdomen or arms can raise blood pressure and ease the symptoms. Tensing the lower body appears to work better than tensing the upper body.
text_ko: 중력이 돌아온 뒤 서 있다가 실신할 것 같은 느낌이 들 때 다리나 배, 팔의 근육에 힘을 주면 혈압이 올라가 증상이 누그러질 수 있다. 상체보다 하체 근육에 힘을 주는 쪽이 더 효과적인 것으로 보인다.

sources.title: 2019 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Focused Update for First Aid: Presyncope (Charlton et al.)

do_not_claim: Abstract-only source (first-aid guidance on Earth, not tested in returning crews). Do not name specific manoeuvres such as leg crossing, squatting or hand gripping, and do not state when the technique should not be used: those details were available only as search summaries.

title_en: The first days after landing
title_ko: 착륙 후 처음 며칠
text_en: Standing tolerance usually returns within one to three days after landing, though some people have symptoms for several days. During that time crews have typically kept the compression garment on, eaten and drunk as tolerated, rested, and put off activities that tend to bring on a drop in blood pressure.
text_ko: 서 있는 자세를 견디는 능력은 대개 착륙 후 하루에서 사흘 사이에 돌아오지만, 며칠 동안 증상이 이어지는 사람도 있다. 그동안 승무원들은 보통 압박복을 계속 착용하고, 무리가 되지 않는 만큼 먹고 마시면서 쉬고, 혈압을 떨어뜨리기 쉬운 활동은 뒤로 미뤄 왔다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations Contributing to Adverse Mission Performance and Health Outcomes
OCHMO-TB-033 Rev C: Spaceflight Experience and Medical Care
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Orthostatic Intolerance During Re-exposure to Gravity

numbers: One day after landing 8 of 9 station astronauts completed the tilt test; on day 3, 13 of 15 station (87%) and 19 of 19 Shuttle astronauts did; some wear compression garments through the first week (NASA HRP Evidence Report on cardiovascular adaptations, 2022). On landing day about 20-30% of short-flight crew were affected on stand or tilt tests, and 5 of 6 (Mir) and 4 of 6 (ISS) long-flight astronauts could not finish a 10-minute tilt (NASA HRP Evidence Report on orthostatic intolerance, 2015).
do_not_claim: Do not quote one incidence percentage without saying that it comes from small tilt-test samples that under-count. Recovery figures are for return to Earth; there are no data for the Mars surface. Treatments given by medical staff after landing are not described here.

title_en: Signs that blood pressure is not holding while upright
title_ko: 서 있을 때 혈압이 유지되지 않는다는 신호
text_en: After gravity returns, signs that blood pressure is not holding while upright can include light-headedness, nausea, narrowing or blurry vision, weakness and a fast heartbeat. These feelings can come before a faint, so they are worth noticing early.
text_ko: 중력이 돌아온 뒤 서 있을 때 혈압이 유지되지 않으면 머리가 아찔하고 메스꺼우며, 시야가 좁아지거나 흐려지고, 기운이 빠지고, 심장이 빨리 뛸 수 있다. 이런 느낌은 실신에 앞서 나타날 수 있으므로 일찍 알아차리는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-033 Rev C: Spaceflight Experience and Medical Care
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Orthostatic Intolerance During Re-exposure to Gravity
Low Blood Pressure
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

numbers: In the test studies near-fainting meant light-headedness, nausea, tunnel vision or a systolic pressure under 70 mmHg (NASA HRP Evidence Report on orthostatic intolerance, 2015).
do_not_claim: These signs are not specific to low blood pressure on standing; do not present them as a diagnosis.

title_en: Situations in which episodes tend to occur
title_ko: 증상이 나타나기 쉬운 상황
text_en: After landing, episodes have been reported while standing still for a long time, in the shower, on the toilet and when walking after a meal. Heat also lowers tolerance of being upright, which is why suits are cooled during entry. These are situations in which to move slowly and keep a seat within reach.
text_ko: 착륙 후에는 오래 가만히 서 있을 때, 샤워할 때, 용변을 볼 때, 식사 뒤에 걸을 때 증상을 겪은 사례가 보고되어 있다. 몸이 더워지면 서 있는 자세를 견디기가 더 어려워지는데, 대기권 진입 때 우주복을 냉각하는 것도 이 때문이다. 이런 상황에서는 천천히 움직이고 앉을 곳을 가까이에 두는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Orthostatic Intolerance During Re-exposure to Gravity
NASA/TM-20205008196: Artemis Sustained Translational Acceleration Limits
Evidence Report: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations Contributing to Adverse Mission Performance and Health Outcomes
Low Blood Pressure
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

numbers: Core temperature ran up to 0.5 °C higher during entry in the protective suit even with liquid cooling (NASA HRP Evidence Report on cardiovascular adaptations, 2022).

title_en: Two sources of dizziness after landing
title_ko: 착륙 후 어지럼의 두 가지 원인
text_en: Dizziness after landing can come from low blood pressure when upright, from the balance system re-adjusting to gravity, or from both. The balance-related kind is described with a spinning sensation, unsteady walking, nausea and vomiting. In testing, a returning crew member has had to stop standing because of this sickness with no sign of low blood pressure.
text_ko: 착륙 후의 어지럼은 서 있을 때 혈압이 낮아져서 생길 수도 있고, 균형 감각이 중력에 다시 적응하는 과정에서 생길 수도 있으며, 두 가지가 겹칠 수도 있다. 균형 감각에서 오는 어지럼은 빙빙 도는 느낌, 불안정한 걸음, 메스꺼움, 구토를 동반한다고 알려져 있다. 실제 검사에서도 혈압이 떨어진 징후 없이 이런 멀미 증상 때문에 서 있기를 중단한 귀환 승무원이 있었다.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-033 Rev C: Spaceflight Experience and Medical Care
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Risk of Altered Sensorimotor and Vestibular Function
Efficacy of Gradient Compression Garments in the Hours After Long-Duration Spaceflight (Lee et al.)
Evidence Report: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations Contributing to Adverse Mission Performance and Health Outcomes

numbers: In 11 station astronauts wearing a gradient compression garment, 3 of 10 could not start the first stand test and one stopped a later test early with motion sickness and no sign of low pressure (Lee et al., Frontiers in Physiology, 2020).
do_not_claim: Do not assign dizziness after landing to one cause from symptoms alone. The clues 'eases on lying down' versus 'set off by head movement' are a researcher inference, not a cited finding.

title_en: Checking blood pressure lying and standing
title_ko: 누웠을 때와 일어섰을 때 혈압 비교하기
text_en: A standard clinical check for this problem compares blood pressure taken after lying down for several minutes with readings taken one and three minutes after standing up. A clear fall in pressure, or light-headedness or dizziness on standing, counts as abnormal. After landing or on the surface, it can serve as a simple recheck when a cuff is available.
text_ko: 이 문제를 확인하는 표준적인 방법은 몇 분간 누워 있다가 잰 혈압을, 일어선 지 일 분 뒤와 삼 분 뒤에 잰 혈압과 비교하는 것이다. 혈압이 뚜렷하게 떨어지거나 일어설 때 머리가 아찔하거나 어지러우면 비정상으로 본다. 착륙 후나 화성 표면에서 혈압계를 쓸 수 있다면 다시 확인하는 방법으로 삼을 수 있다.

sources.title: STEADI: Measuring Orthostatic Blood Pressure
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

numbers: Lie down for 5 minutes, then stand; a fall of 20 mmHg or more in systolic or 10 mmHg or more in diastolic pressure at 1 or 3 minutes, or light-headedness or dizziness, counts as abnormal (CDC STEADI, Measuring Orthostatic Blood Pressure, 2017).
do_not_claim: This is an Earth clinical measuring rule; the notes contain no evidence that its thresholds have been tested in returning crews.

title_en: When dizziness after landing needs medical contact
title_ko: 착륙 후 어지럼으로 의료진에게 알려야 할 때
text_en: Contact the CMO or ground medical staff immediately if dizziness or faintness after landing comes with cold, sweaty or bluish skin, fast breathing, a weak, fast pulse, chest pain or trouble breathing. These signs point beyond a simple drop in blood pressure on standing and should not be waited out.
text_ko: 착륙 후 어지럼이나 실신할 것 같은 느낌과 함께 피부가 차갑고 식은땀이 나거나, 피부색이 푸르스름해지거나, 호흡이 빨라지거나, 맥박이 약하고 빠르거나, 가슴 통증이나 숨참이 있으면 즉시 CMO나 지상 의료진에게 알려야 한다. 이런 징후는 일어설 때 혈압이 잠깐 떨어지는 정도를 넘어서는 문제일 수 있으므로, 나아지기를 기다려서는 안 된다.

sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

sources.title: Arrhythmias: Symptoms
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

sources.title: About Heart Attack Symptoms, Risk, and Recovery
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

do_not_claim: Not a diagnosis. The red-flag list for fainting itself (for example not coming round within minutes, or injury in the fall) existed only in an excluded source, so it is not stated here.

title_en: What the heart-rate jump on standing can and cannot tell
title_ko: 일어설 때 심박수 상승이 알려 주는 것과 알려 주지 못하는 것
text_en: Heart rate normally rises on standing, and on landing day the rise is larger than before flight. A bigger jump is not by itself a bad sign: in a ground test, people whose blood pressure held raised their heart rate more than those near fainting. Heart rate alone therefore cannot show how serious an episode is.
text_ko: 심박수는 일어서면 원래 올라가며, 착륙 당일에는 비행 전보다 더 크게 오른다. 그러나 많이 오르는 것 자체가 나쁜 신호는 아니다. 지상 시험에서는 혈압을 유지한 사람들이 실신할 뻔한 사람들보다 심박수가 더 많이 올랐으므로, 심박수만으로는 증상이 얼마나 심한지 알 수 없다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Orthostatic Intolerance During Re-exposure to Gravity
NASA/TM-20205008196: Artemis Sustained Translational Acceleration Limits

numbers: Rise in heart rate on standing or tilt: about +18 beats/min before flight; about +30 on landing day after short and medium Shuttle flights and +25 after 15-17-day flights (NASA/TM-20205008196, 2020). In a ground model of landing-day low volume, people who nearly fainted rose about 30 beats/min while systolic pressure fell about 32 mmHg; those who coped rose about 43 and held pressure (NASA HRP Evidence Report on orthostatic intolerance, 2015).
do_not_claim: Do not say that a higher or lower heart-rate jump tells severity, and do not say that a wearable can detect or predict fainting: no wearable signal has been validated for this.

title_en: Resting heart rate after gravity returns
title_ko: 중력이 돌아온 뒤의 안정 시 심박수
text_en: Resting heart rate can sit above a person's usual level for the first days after gravity returns and then settle. The same rise can go with fever, too little fluid, a short spell of hard training or too much caffeine, so a higher resting rate cannot show which of these is present.
text_ko: 안정 시 심박수는 중력이 돌아온 뒤 처음 며칠 동안 평소 수준보다 높게 유지되다가 가라앉을 수 있다. 열이 날 때, 몸에 수분이 모자랄 때, 짧은 기간 강도 높은 훈련을 했을 때, 카페인을 너무 많이 섭취했을 때도 똑같이 오를 수 있다. 따라서 안정 시 심박수가 높다는 것만으로는 그 원인이 무엇인지 알 수 없다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Orthostatic Intolerance During Re-exposure to Gravity
Feasibility of continuous fever monitoring using wearable devices (Smarr et al.)
Autonomic adaptations mediate the effect of hydration on brain functioning and mood (Young et al.)
Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of the Overtraining Syndrome: ECSS/ACSM Joint Consensus Statement (Meeusen et al.)
Caffeine (health topic)

numbers: 13 of 21 Apollo astronauts had a higher resting heart rate after flight, back to the pre-flight level by 2-3 days; after Shuttle flights heart rate returned to pre-flight values within an hour of landing (NASA HRP Evidence Report on orthostatic intolerance, 2015). Short training overload raised resting rate by about 4.5 beats/min (Meeusen et al., 2013). About 6 beats/min faster with mild fluid loss in heat (Young et al., 2019; two small trials).
do_not_claim: Do not say that resting heart rate is known to rise or to fall in orbit (sources disagree), and do not say that a wearable can tell the cause of a rise.

title_en: Why crews tend to drink too little in flight
title_ko: 비행 중에 물을 적게 마시게 되는 이유
text_en: In flight, crew members typically drink less than before flight and often less than the recommended amount, possibly because thirst is reduced. This raises the risk of dehydration, and it means thirst may not be a dependable reminder to drink.
text_ko: 비행 중 승무원은 대체로 비행 전보다 물을 적게 마시고 권장량에 못 미치는 경우도 많은데, 갈증을 덜 느끼기 때문일 수 있다. 그만큼 탈수 위험이 커지며, 갈증이 날 때만 마시면 필요한 양을 채우지 못할 수 있다.

sources.title: Human Adaptation to Spaceflight: The Role of Food and Nutrition, 2nd edition
OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B: Water - Human Consumption
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Health Outcomes and Decrements in Performance due to In-Flight Medical Conditions

numbers: Average daily water intake (drinks plus water added to food): Apollo about 1.6 L, Skylab about 2.8 L, Shuttle about 2.2 L, ISS about 2.0-2.3 L (NASA OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B, 2023). In ISS data 40% of astronauts met a sports-medicine definition of dehydration (urine osmolality above 700 mOsm/kg) and 8.7% a clinical one (serum sodium above 145 mmol/L); the caption does not say whether these are in-flight samples only (NASA, Human Adaptation to Spaceflight, 2021, Figure 21). Recorded as a medical event, dehydration was rare: 2 entries through ISS Expedition 40 (NASA HRP Evidence Report on in-flight medical conditions, 2017; old data).
do_not_claim: Do not say that weightlessness itself dehydrates the body or causes a proven increase in urination: sources disagree. The cause of the reduced thirst is unknown.

title_en: Dehydration and kidney stones
title_ko: 탈수와 신장 결석
text_en: Without preventive measures, dehydration together with extra calcium leaving the bones can raise the risk of kidney stones during spaceflight. Drinking enough is described as the simplest non-drug way to lower that risk.
text_ko: 별다른 대비가 없으면 탈수에 더해 뼈에서 빠져나오는 칼슘이 늘어나 우주 비행 중 신장 결석 위험이 커질 수 있다. 물을 충분히 마시는 것은 약을 쓰지 않고 이 위험을 낮추는 가장 쉬운 방법으로 꼽힌다.

sources.title: Hazard: Gravity Fields
Evidence Report: Risk of Renal Stone Formation
Human Adaptation to Spaceflight: The Role of Food and Nutrition, 2nd edition

numbers: Kidney-stone risk rises when urine volume is under 1.5 L/day; a good hydration countermeasure yields 2.5-3 L/day of urine; modelling suggests an intake of about 3.2 L/day to reach the pre-flight calcium-oxalate risk by fluid alone (NASA HRP Evidence Report on renal stone formation, 2024).
do_not_claim: Do not name or suggest any stone-prevention medicine.

title_en: How mild dehydration affects thinking and performance
title_ko: 가벼운 탈수가 판단력과 수행 능력에 미치는 영향
text_en: A water deficit of only two to three percent of body weight is linked to poorer concentration and decision-making and to lower physical performance. Mild under-hydration is also linked to worse tolerance of standing upright, which matters most when gravity returns.
text_ko: 체중의 이삼 퍼센트에 해당하는 수분만 잃어도 집중력과 판단력이 떨어지고 신체 수행 능력이 낮아질 수 있다. 가벼운 수분 부족은 서 있는 자세를 견디는 능력도 떨어뜨리는 것으로 알려져 있어, 중력이 돌아오는 시기에는 더 문제가 될 수 있다.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B: Water - Human Consumption
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Human Adaptation to Spaceflight: The Role of Food and Nutrition, 2nd edition
Hydration Status and Cardiovascular Function (Watso & Farquhar)

numbers: Losing 2.5% of body weight as water impairs decision-making and concentration and cuts physical performance potential by 35% (NASA OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B, 2023, crediting a military nutrition guide); cognition suffers when the deficit exceeds 2% of body mass (NASA, Human Adaptation to Spaceflight, 2021). Severity bands: mild 1-5% of body mass, moderate 5-10%, severe above 10% (Watso & Farquhar, Nutrients, 2019).
do_not_claim: The 2% and 2.5% thresholds come from sports and military guidance, not from measurements in spaceflight, and the sources set the threshold slightly differently.

title_en: Signs that can go with dehydration
title_ko: 탈수 때 나타날 수 있는 증상
text_en: Signs that can go with dehydration include strong thirst, a dry mouth, passing less and darker urine, headache, tiredness, dizziness, sleepiness and trouble concentrating. When they appear, it helps to check how much one has drunk that day.
text_ko: 탈수가 있으면 심한 갈증, 입 마름, 소변량 감소와 짙어진 소변 색, 두통, 피로, 어지럼, 졸림, 집중력 저하 같은 증상이 나타날 수 있다. 이런 증상이 있을 때는 그날 물을 얼마나 마셨는지를 함께 살펴보는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B: Water - Human Consumption
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Dehydration (health topic)

do_not_claim: These signs also have other causes; do not present them as proof of dehydration.

title_en: Days on which dehydration is more likely
title_ko: 탈수가 생기기 쉬운 날
text_en: Dehydration is more likely when exercise lasts longer than an hour, when working in heat, on spacewalk days, and during illness with vomiting, diarrhoea or fever. Too much caffeine can add to fluid loss. These are the days on which to keep a closer eye on drinking.
text_ko: 운동을 한 시간 넘게 할 때, 더운 환경에서 일할 때, 선외 활동을 하는 날, 그리고 구토나 설사, 발열을 동반한 병을 앓을 때는 탈수가 생기기 쉽다. 카페인을 지나치게 많이 섭취해도 수분 손실이 늘 수 있다. 이런 날에는 물을 제대로 마시고 있는지 더 자주 살펴보는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B: Water - Human Consumption
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Dehydration (health topic)
NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 Revision C: Crew Health
Caffeine (health topic)

numbers: Listed routes to dehydration include exercising for more than 60 minutes; the vehicle water standard adds 240 mL per hour of spacewalk (NASA OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B, 2023).
do_not_claim: Do not say that caffeine in normal amounts dehydrates crew members: only 'too much' is sourced.

title_en: Urine volume in flight
title_ko: 비행 중 소변량
text_en: Long-duration crews have passed markedly less urine in flight than before flight. A low urine volume is linked to a higher chance of kidney stones, which is one reason to keep track of urine and fluid intake together.
text_ko: 장기 체류 승무원은 비행 중 소변량이 비행 전보다 뚜렷하게 적었다. 소변량이 적으면 신장 결석이 생길 가능성이 커지므로, 소변 상태와 마신 물의 양을 함께 기록해 두는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Renal Stone Formation

numbers: Urine output in long-duration crew was 47% lower before flight day 30 and 39% lower after day 60 than before flight; stone risk rises when urine volume is under 1.5 L/day (NASA HRP Evidence Report on renal stone formation, 2024).
do_not_claim: Do not judge in-flight urine volume against pre-flight habits without noting that output is lower in flight for crews in general.

title_en: What to drink for mild dehydration
title_ko: 가벼운 탈수일 때 마실 것
text_en: For mild dehydration the main step is to drink water. A drink containing electrolytes can help when salts have been lost as well, for example after heavy sweating.
text_ko: 가벼운 탈수라면 우선 물을 마시는 것이 기본이다. 땀을 많이 흘린 뒤처럼 전해질도 함께 빠져나갔을 때는 전해질이 든 음료가 도움이 될 수 있다.

sources.title: Dehydration (health topic)

do_not_claim: Do not advise adding salt routinely in flight: sodium intake is otherwise limited, and salt loading belongs only to the prescribed fluid load before landing.

title_en: How much to drink each day
title_ko: 하루에 마셔야 할 양
text_en: Fluid requirements written for space crews all call for more than about two litres a day, with extra on spacewalk days; the exact figure depends on body size and purpose. Holding back on drinking to save water is discouraged, and drinking too much is considered very unlikely to cause harm in flight.
text_ko: 우주 승무원을 위한 수분 섭취 기준은 모두 하루 두 리터가 넘는 양을 요구하며, 선외 활동을 하는 날에는 더 마시도록 한다. 정확한 양은 체격과 목적에 따라 달라진다. 물을 아끼려고 마시는 양을 줄이는 것은 권장되지 않으며, 비행 중에 물을 지나치게 많이 마셔서 문제가 생길 가능성은 매우 낮은 것으로 본다.

sources.title: Human Adaptation to Spaceflight: The Role of Food and Nutrition, 2nd edition
OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B: Water - Human Consumption
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Renal Stone Formation

numbers: Fluid requirement: more than 2,000 mL/day (ISS 1996, exploration 2005); 32 mL per kg body weight, with more than 2,100 mL for women and more than 2,500 mL for men (exploration 2020) (NASA, Human Adaptation to Spaceflight, 2021, Table 1). Vehicle standard: at least 2.5 L of potable water per crew member per day for hydration, plus 240 mL per hour of spacewalk (NASA OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B, 2023). Kidney-stone modelling suggests about 3.2 L/day (NASA HRP Evidence Report on renal stone formation, 2024).
do_not_claim: Do not present one litres-per-day figure as 'the' requirement: 2.0, 2.1/2.5, 2.5 and about 3.2 L are given for different purposes.

title_en: Drinking during motion sickness early in flight
title_ko: 비행 초기 멀미 중의 수분 섭취
text_en: Motion sickness is common in the first days of flight, and vomiting adds to fluid loss. Continuing to drink in amounts that keep up hydration is encouraged; when fluid is hard to keep down, small sips are easier to tolerate.
text_ko: 비행 초기 며칠 동안은 멀미가 흔하며, 구토를 하면 수분이 더 빠져나간다. 이때도 몸에 수분이 모자라지 않을 만큼 계속 마시는 것이 권장되며, 속이 받지 않을 때는 한 모금씩 나누어 마시면 한결 수월하다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Renal Stone Formation
OCHMO-TB-033 Rev C: Spaceflight Experience and Medical Care
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Dehydration (health topic)

numbers: Motion sickness affects 50-70% of crew in the first days of flight (NASA OCHMO-TB-033 Rev C, 2023).
do_not_claim: For severe early motion sickness, fluid given by medical staff may be considered; that decision belongs to the CMO and ground medical staff. Do not advise extra salt.

title_en: Higher body temperature and exercise in space
title_ko: 우주에서 높아지는 체온과 운동
text_en: Body temperature runs higher in space, at rest after the first months and especially during exercise, and this may raise fluid needs. Extra drinking water is allotted for spacewalks, and drinking more around long exercise sessions is sensible too.
text_ko: 우주에서는 체온이 지상에서보다 높게 유지되는데, 처음 몇 달이 지나면 쉬고 있을 때도 그렇고 운동 중에는 더욱 그렇다. 이 때문에 필요한 수분량이 늘 수 있다. 선외 활동에는 마실 물이 추가로 배정되며, 오래 운동하는 날에도 평소보다 더 마시는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: Increased core body temperature in astronauts during long-duration space missions (Stahn et al.)
OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B: Water - Human Consumption
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Dehydration (health topic)
Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness

numbers: In 11 astronauts resting core temperature rose by about 1 °C over the first 2.5 months, and peak temperature during exercise was about 1.4 °C higher than on the ground, exceeding 40 °C in some (Stahn et al., Scientific Reports, 2017). An extra 240 mL of water per hour of spacewalk (NASA OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B, 2023). Station crews exercise 1.5 hours a day, 6-7 days a week (NASA, Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness, 2025).
do_not_claim: No source gives an amount to drink around in-flight exercise sessions, and fluid lost as sweat on the station was not measured.

title_en: When dehydration needs medical contact
title_ko: 탈수로 의료진에게 알려야 할 때
text_en: Contact the CMO or ground medical staff immediately if suspected dehydration comes with confusion, fainting, no urine at all, a rapid heartbeat or rapid breathing. Severe dehydration needs treatment from the medical team; drinking alone is not enough.
text_ko: 탈수가 의심되는 상황에서 정신이 혼란스럽거나, 실신하거나, 소변이 전혀 나오지 않거나, 심장이 빨리 뛰거나, 호흡이 빨라지면 즉시 CMO나 지상 의료진에게 알려야 한다. 심한 탈수는 물을 마시는 것만으로 해결되지 않으며 의료진의 처치가 필요하다.

sources.title: Dehydration (health topic)

do_not_claim: Not a diagnosis. Do not describe the treatment itself.

title_en: Fluid redistribution is not the same as dehydration
title_ko: 체액 재분포는 탈수와 다르다
text_en: Early in weightlessness the volume of blood plasma falls, and it then stays somewhat lower than before flight. This is mainly a redistribution of body fluid, not simply a shortage of water. Sources differ on whether the early fluid shift also causes extra urination.
text_ko: 무중력 초기에는 혈액 속 혈장의 양이 줄어들고, 그 뒤로도 비행 전보다 다소 적은 상태가 이어진다. 이는 단순히 물이 부족해서가 아니라 주로 체액이 몸 안에서 다시 분포하기 때문이다. 초기의 체액 이동이 소변량까지 늘리는지에 대해서는 자료마다 설명이 다르다.

sources.title: Human Adaptation to Spaceflight: The Role of Food and Nutrition, 2nd edition
OCHMO-TB-033 Rev C: Spaceflight Experience and Medical Care
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Orthostatic Intolerance During Re-exposure to Gravity

numbers: Plasma volume about 17% below pre-flight within hours, about 11% below after roughly 8-12 days and 10-15% below on long flights, while total body water falls only about 1% (NASA, Human Adaptation to Spaceflight, 2021). A medical brief instead describes a 12-15% reduction in 'whole body volume' with temporary heavy urination in the first days (NASA OCHMO-TB-033 Rev C, 2023).
do_not_claim: Do not say that weightlessness 'dehydrates' the body or causes a proven increase in urination, and do not say that it does not: sources disagree. A puffy face or stuffy head reflects the normal fluid shift toward the head, not too much fluid.

title_en: What heart signals can and cannot tell about hydration
title_ko: 심박 신호가 수분 상태에 대해 알려 주는 것과 알려 주지 못하는 것
text_en: In small trials on Earth, mild fluid loss in a warm room went with a slightly faster heartbeat and lower heart-rate variability than when water was given. No in-flight study linking hydration to wearable readings has been identified, so these signals cannot show that a person is dehydrated.
text_ko: 지상에서 이루어진 소규모 시험에서는 더운 방에서 수분을 조금 잃었을 때 물을 마신 경우보다 심장이 약간 빨리 뛰고 심박 변이도가 낮았다. 그러나 수분 상태와 착용형 기기 측정값의 관계를 비행 중에 살펴본 연구는 아직 알려진 것이 없으므로, 이런 신호만으로 탈수 여부를 알 수는 없다.

sources.title: Autonomic adaptations mediate the effect of hydration on brain functioning and mood (Young et al.)

numbers: Two randomised trials (12 and 56 young adults, four hours in a 30 °C room without water, about 0.6% body-mass loss): heartbeat about 6 beats/min faster and lower SDNN and RMSSD than when 300 mL of water was given (Young et al., Scientific Reports, 2019; small samples, part beverage-industry funding).
do_not_claim: Do not say that a wearable can measure hydration or detect dehydration. The evidence is from small ground trials in heat and is low-confidence.

title_en: What skin temperature can tell: compare with one's own baseline
title_ko: 피부 온도가 알려 주는 것: 자신의 기준선과 비교
text_en: Skin temperature from a wearable differs widely between people, in both its average and its range, and it changes with the time of day. No fixed cut-off applies: a reading is meaningful only against the same person's baseline, and only when compared with values taken at a similar time of day.
text_ko: 착용형 기기로 잰 피부 온도는 평균도 변동 폭도 사람마다 크게 다르고, 하루 중 시간대에 따라서도 달라진다. 따라서 모든 사람에게 똑같이 적용할 수 있는 기준값은 없다. 피부 온도는 그 사람 자신의 기준선과 비교해야 하고, 그것도 비슷한 시간대에 잰 값끼리 비교해야 의미가 있다.

sources.title: Feasibility of continuous fever monitoring using wearable devices (Smarr et al.)

do_not_claim: Do not treat skin temperature as body (core) temperature and do not apply a fixed fever cut-off. The study used a finger-ring sensor on Earth; wrist skin temperature has not been validated in astronauts. Menstrual-cycle phase also shifts skin temperature and has to be taken into account.

title_en: What skin temperature cannot tell
title_ko: 피부 온도가 알려 주지 못하는 것
text_en: In one study on Earth, skin temperature ran a little above personal baseline around the start of an infection in most participants, yet the same rule also flagged people with no fever and missed some with fever. A rise is a reason to look for a cause, not a sign that fever, infection or dehydration is present.
text_ko: 지상에서 이루어진 한 연구에서는 감염이 시작될 무렵 참가자 대부분의 피부 온도가 개인 기준선보다 조금 높았다. 그러나 같은 판정 기준이 열이 없었던 사람을 발열로 잘못 가려내기도 하고 열이 있었던 사람 일부를 놓치기도 했다. 피부 온도가 올랐다면 원인을 찾아볼 이유는 되지만, 그것만으로 발열이나 감염, 탈수가 있다고 볼 수는 없다.

sources.title: Feasibility of continuous fever monitoring using wearable devices (Smarr et al.)
Increased core body temperature in astronauts during long-duration space missions (Stahn et al.)

numbers: 50 people with COVID-19 wearing a finger-ring sensor: skin temperature around symptom onset averaged 0.63 °C above personal baseline (± 1 °C); 38 (76%) had fever-like days before reporting symptoms; the rule flagged 7 of 12 who reported no fever and missed 3 of 38 who did (Smarr et al., Scientific Reports, 2020; proof of concept, device-maker funded). In space, resting core temperature runs about 1 °C higher after the first 2.5 months, measured at the forehead and not at the wrist (Stahn et al., Scientific Reports, 2017).
do_not_claim: Whether skin temperature changes with dehydration has not been established. Do not say that a wearable has detected a fever or an infection.

title_en: What is known about heart problems in spaceflight
title_ko: 우주 비행 중 심장 문제에 대해 알려진 것
text_en: Crews are carefully screened and documented heart problems in space are few, yet heart-rhythm disturbances and symptoms of reduced blood supply to the heart have still been reported in flight. Whether spaceflight itself causes rhythm problems or makes them more frequent is not settled.
text_ko: 승무원은 엄격한 선발 검진을 거치고 우주에서 기록된 심장 문제도 많지 않지만, 비행 중에 부정맥이나 심장으로 가는 혈류가 부족할 때의 증상이 보고된 적이 있다. 우주 비행 자체가 부정맥을 일으키거나 더 잦게 만드는지는 아직 결론이 나지 않았다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations Contributing to Adverse Mission Performance and Health Outcomes
Evidence Report: Risk of Cardiac Rhythm Problems During Spaceflight
Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations

numbers: Mir over 11 years: 0.07 significant medical events per person-year, 30 first reports of rhythm or conduction abnormalities, and one early return in 1987 for a persistent fast rhythm (NASA HRP Evidence Report on cardiac rhythm problems, 2017). Holter monitoring on 4-16-day Shuttle flights found about the same frequency of rhythm disturbances as before flight (NASA HRP Evidence Report on cardiovascular adaptations, 2022).
do_not_claim: Do not say that spaceflight causes arrhythmias or heart attacks (inconclusive), and do not say that screened astronauts cannot have a cardiac event.

title_en: Why the crew must respond first on a Mars mission
title_ko: 화성 임무에서 승무원이 먼저 대응해야 하는 이유
text_en: On a Mars mission a signal can take up to about twenty minutes one way, so ground medical staff cannot follow a heart problem as it happens. For that reason Mars crews are to receive more training to deal with serious heart problems themselves, and the first decisions rest with the crew on site.
text_ko: 화성 임무에서는 신호가 한쪽으로 가는 데에만 최대 이십 분쯤 걸릴 수 있어, 지상 의료진이 심장 문제를 실시간으로 지켜볼 수 없다. 그래서 화성 승무원은 심각한 심장 문제에 스스로 대처하는 훈련을 더 받게 되며, 첫 판단과 대응은 현장에 있는 승무원의 몫이 된다.

sources.title: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
Hazard: Distance From Earth
Evidence Report: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations Contributing to Adverse Mission Performance and Health Outcomes

numbers: One-way communication delay to Mars: up to 20 minutes (NASA, Hazard: Distance From Earth).

title_en: The tendency to explain heart symptoms away
title_ko: 심장 증상을 대수롭지 않게 넘기려는 경향
text_en: A crew member may be reluctant to believe that symptoms come from the heart, out of concern for the mission or trust in pre-flight screening. Symptoms might also appear only during exertion. Both are reasons to report chest symptoms early and not explain them away.
text_ko: 승무원은 임무에 지장을 줄까 걱정하거나 비행 전 검진 결과를 믿는 마음에서, 자신의 증상이 심장에서 온 것이라고 받아들이기를 꺼릴 수 있다. 또 증상이 몸을 많이 쓸 때에만 나타날 수도 있다. 그러므로 가슴에 증상이 있으면 대수롭지 않게 넘기지 말고 일찍 알리는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Cardiac Rhythm Problems During Spaceflight
Heart Attack: Symptoms
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

do_not_claim: Do not reassure on the grounds that the crew member passed screening.

title_en: Heart-attack symptoms are not always sudden or severe
title_ko: 심근경색 증상이 항상 갑작스럽고 심한 것은 아니다
text_en: Heart-attack symptoms are not always sudden or severe: they can build slowly, stay mild, or come and go over several hours, and some people have none. Chest pain from reduced blood supply to the heart often follows exertion and eases with rest, whereas heart-attack pain does not ease with rest.
text_ko: 심근경색의 증상이 항상 갑작스럽고 심하게 나타나는 것은 아니다. 서서히 심해지거나, 약하게만 나타나거나, 몇 시간에 걸쳐 나타났다 사라지기를 되풀이할 수 있고, 증상이 전혀 없는 경우도 있다. 심장으로 가는 혈류가 부족해서 생기는 가슴 통증은 흔히 몸을 쓴 뒤에 나타나 쉬면 가라앉지만, 심근경색의 통증은 쉬어도 가라앉지 않는다.

sources.title: Heart Attack: Symptoms
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

do_not_claim: Pain that eases with rest is not thereby harmless; do not use this difference to reassure or to diagnose.

title_en: How a heart-rhythm problem can feel
title_ko: 부정맥은 어떻게 느껴질 수 있는가
text_en: A heart-rhythm problem can be felt as a skipped beat, a fluttering, pounding or racing heart, or a slow or irregular beat with pauses. It can also bring tiredness, dizziness, fainting or anxiety, or cause no symptoms at all.
text_ko: 부정맥이 있으면 가슴 두근거림을 느낄 수 있는데, 심장이 한 박자 건너뛰거나, 파르르 떨리거나, 쿵쿵 뛰거나, 지나치게 빨리 뛰는 느낌이 여기에 해당한다. 맥이 느리거나 불규칙하고 잠깐 멈추는 듯할 수도 있으며, 피로나 어지럼, 실신, 불안이 따르거나 아무 증상이 없을 수도 있다.

sources.title: Arrhythmias: Symptoms
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

do_not_claim: Do not say that a wearable has detected an irregular rhythm.

title_en: Report first, do not wait
title_ko: 기다리지 말고 먼저 알리기
text_en: With symptoms that could come from the heart, the most useful thing a crew member can do is report them without waiting to see whether they pass, because earlier treatment limits damage to the heart muscle. Reporting comes first; it should not be put off in order to take a medicine on one's own.
text_ko: 심장에서 온 것일 수 있는 증상이 있을 때 승무원이 할 수 있는 가장 중요한 일은 저절로 가라앉는지 지켜보며 기다리지 않고 알리는 것이다. 치료가 빠를수록 심장 근육의 손상을 줄일 수 있기 때문이다. 알리는 것이 먼저이며, 혼자 판단해 약을 먹느라 알리는 일을 미뤄서는 안 된다.

title_en: Chest pain or pressure: contact the CMO at once
title_ko: 가슴 통증이나 압박감이 있으면 곧바로 알리기
text_en: Contact the CMO and ground medical staff immediately for chest pain or discomfort, felt as pressure, squeezing, fullness or pain in the centre or left side of the chest, that lasts more than a few minutes or goes away and comes back. Do not wait to see whether it settles.
text_ko: 가슴 한가운데나 왼쪽이 짓눌리거나 조이거나 꽉 찬 듯하거나 아픈 느낌이 몇 분 넘게 이어지거나 사라졌다가 다시 나타나면 즉시 CMO와 지상 의료진에게 알려야 한다. 가라앉는지 지켜보며 기다려서는 안 된다.

title_en: Other possible heart-attack symptoms
title_ko: 심근경색일 수 있는 그 밖의 증상
text_en: Treat these as possible heart-attack symptoms and contact the CMO and ground medical staff immediately: pain or discomfort in the jaw, neck, back, or one or both arms or shoulders; shortness of breath, with or before chest discomfort; or weakness, light-headedness or a cold sweat. Unusual tiredness, nausea or vomiting can be symptoms too.
text_ko: 턱이나 목, 등, 한쪽 또는 양쪽 팔과 어깨가 아프거나 불편할 때, 가슴 불편감과 함께 또는 그보다 먼저 숨이 찰 때, 기운이 빠지거나 머리가 아찔하거나 식은땀이 날 때는 심근경색의 증상일 수 있으므로 즉시 CMO와 지상 의료진에게 알려야 한다. 평소와 다른 심한 피로나 메스꺼움, 구토도 증상일 수 있다.

title_en: Racing or irregular heartbeat with other symptoms
title_ko: 다른 증상을 동반한 빠르거나 불규칙한 심장 박동
text_en: Contact the CMO and ground medical staff immediately if a racing, pounding or irregular heartbeat comes with chest pain or difficulty breathing. Do the same for sudden dizziness, heavy sweating without a clear reason, or breathlessness at rest, and for cold, sweaty or bluish skin with a weak, fast pulse.
text_ko: 심장이 지나치게 빨리 뛰거나 쿵쿵거리거나 불규칙하게 뛰면서 가슴 통증이나 숨참이 함께 있으면 즉시 CMO와 지상 의료진에게 알려야 한다. 갑작스러운 어지럼이 있거나, 뚜렷한 이유 없이 땀이 많이 나거나, 가만히 있어도 숨이 찰 때, 그리고 피부가 차갑고 식은땀이 나거나 푸르스름하면서 맥박이 약하고 빠를 때도 마찬가지다.

title_en: Limits of wrist heart-rate readings
title_ko: 손목 심박수 측정의 한계
text_en: Wrist devices estimate heart rate from light-based readings of blood flow under the skin. Averages can be accurate, but any single reading may be far off, especially with wrist movement or a loose fit. Such devices cannot replace a medical-grade heart recording, so a normal-looking number does not settle whether the heart is the problem.
text_ko: 손목에 차는 기기는 피부 아래 혈류를 빛으로 읽어 심박수를 추정한다. 평균값은 정확할 수 있지만, 손목을 움직이거나 기기가 헐겁게 채워져 있으면 개별 측정값은 실제와 크게 다를 수 있다. 이런 기기는 의료용 심전도 기록을 대신할 수 없으므로, 수치가 정상으로 보인다고 해서 심장에 문제가 없다고 단정할 수는 없다.

sources.title: Guidelines for wrist-worn consumer wearable assessment of heart rate in biobehavioral research (Nelson et al.)
Investigating sources of inaccuracy in wearable optical heart rate sensors (Bent et al.)

numbers: Against an ECG patch in 53 people across six devices: mean absolute error at rest about 7 beats/min for consumer devices (best 4.4) and about 14 for research-grade ones, with error about 30% higher during activity (Bent et al., npj Digital Medicine, 2020).
do_not_claim: Do not say that the wearable has detected or ruled out an arrhythmia or a heart attack. A report of chest pain or breathlessness is acted on whatever the wearable shows.

title_en: Resting heart rate: compare with one's own usual level
title_ko: 안정 시 심박수: 자신의 평소 수준과 비교
text_en: Resting heart rate differs widely between healthy people, but within one person it usually shifts only a little from week to week. A change from one's own usual level is therefore more informative than a comparison with a general range, although its value for medical decisions has not been shown.
text_ko: 안정 시 심박수는 건강한 사람 사이에서도 차이가 크지만, 같은 사람에게서는 주마다 조금씩만 달라지는 것이 보통이다. 따라서 일반적인 범위와 견주기보다 자신의 평소 수준에서 얼마나 달라졌는지를 보는 편이 더 많은 것을 알려 준다. 다만 이런 변화가 의학적 판단에 실제로 쓸모가 있는지는 아직 입증되지 않았다.

sources.title: Inter- and intraindividual variability in daily resting heart rate and its associations with age, sex, sleep, BMI, and time of year (Quer et al.)

numbers: 92,457 wrist-tracker users followed for a median of 320 days: mean daily resting rate 65.5 ± 7.7 beats/min, individual averages about 40-109; median week-to-week swing about 3 beats/min; about 20% had at least one week with a swing of 10 or more; about 2 beats/min higher in mid-winter than in mid-summer (Quer et al., PLOS ONE, 2020).
do_not_claim: Do not state a 'normal' resting range (that figure existed only in an excluded source), and do not say that a resting heart rate at one's usual level rules out a heart problem.

title_en: What heart-rate variability is
title_ko: 심박 변이도란 무엇인가
text_en: Heart-rate variability is the variation in time between one heartbeat and the next. It falls with age and with a faster heart rate, and it shifts with breathing, posture and time of day, so readings can be compared only when taken the same way, and best against one's own earlier readings.
text_ko: 심박 변이도(HRV)는 한 번의 심장 박동과 다음 박동 사이의 시간 간격이 얼마나 달라지는지를 나타낸다. 나이가 들수록, 심박수가 빠를수록 낮아지고 호흡이나 자세, 하루 중 시간대에 따라서도 달라진다. 그래서 같은 방식으로 잰 값끼리만 비교할 수 있으며, 자신의 이전 측정값과 견주어 보는 것이 가장 좋다.

sources.title: An Overview of Heart Rate Variability Metrics and Norms (Shaffer & Ginsberg)

numbers: Short-recording norms in healthy adults (review of 44 studies, 21,438 people): SDNN about 50 ± 16 ms, RMSSD about 42 ± 15 ms; values from 24-hour, 5-minute and shorter recordings are not interchangeable (Shaffer & Ginsberg, Frontiers in Public Health, 2017).
do_not_claim: Do not compare heart-rate variability values across devices, body positions or recording lengths.

title_en: What heart-rate variability cannot tell
title_ko: 심박 변이도가 알려 주지 못하는 것
text_en: Small drops in heart-rate variability have been seen after sleep loss, with mild fluid loss and during fever-like illness, but the effects are small, inconsistent and overlapping. A higher value is not always better either: an irregular heart rhythm or a single misread beat can inflate the number, so a high value should not be taken as reassurance.
text_ko: 잠을 제대로 자지 못한 뒤, 몸에서 수분이 조금 빠져나갔을 때, 열이 나는 병을 앓을 때 심박 변이도가 약간 낮아진 사례가 보고되었지만, 그 변화는 작고 연구마다 일정하지 않으며 서로 겹친다. 값이 높다고 해서 반드시 좋은 것도 아니다. 불규칙한 심장 리듬이나 한 번의 박동 인식 오류만으로도 수치가 부풀 수 있으므로, 높은 값을 심장이 괜찮다는 근거로 삼아서는 안 된다.

sources.title: An Overview of Heart Rate Variability Metrics and Norms (Shaffer & Ginsberg)
Effects of sleep deprivation on heart rate variability (Zhang et al.)
Autonomic adaptations mediate the effect of hydration on brain functioning and mood (Young et al.)
Feasibility of continuous fever monitoring using wearable devices (Smarr et al.)
Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of the Overtraining Syndrome: ECSS/ACSM Joint Consensus Statement (Meeusen et al.)
Evidence Report: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations Contributing to Adverse Mission Performance and Health Outcomes

numbers: Sleep deprivation: small drop in RMSSD (standardised difference -0.24, 95% CI -0.47 to 0.00; 11 trials, 549 participants) and no significant change in SDNN (Zhang et al., Frontiers in Neurology, 2025). In overreached or overtrained athletes the results are inconsistent (Meeusen et al., 2013).
do_not_claim: Do not say that the low-to-high-frequency ratio shows 'stress balance', that higher heart-rate variability always means better recovery, or that overtraining can be detected from it. Findings in spaceflight are mixed.

title_en: First steps for acute chest pain (summary of an older space station medical checklist)
title_ko: 갑자기 가슴 통증이 생겼을 때 먼저 하는 일 (옛 우주정거장 의료 점검표 요약)
text_en: For a crew member with sudden chest pain, the first step is to give oxygen through a mask.
text_ko: 갑자기 가슴 통증이 생긴 승무원에게는 먼저 산소 마스크로 산소를 준다.

title_en: Ask about the pain and write it down
title_ko: 통증을 묻고 적기
text_en: Ask about the pain and write it down: where it is, whether it spreads or stays in one place, how strong it is on a scale of one to ten, whether it is constant or comes and goes, how long it has lasted, and whether it feels sharp, burning or like pressure.
text_ko: 통증을 묻고 적는다. 어디가 아픈지, 다른 곳으로 퍼지는지 한곳에 머무는지, 일에서 십까지의 눈금으로 얼마나 센지, 계속되는지 나타났다 사라지는지, 얼마나 오래됐는지, 찌르는 듯한지 타는 듯한지 누르는 듯한지를 적는다.

numbers: Severity scale 1-10, 10 being worst (JSC-48522-E4, Chest Pain - Acute, step 2).

title_en: Measure and record vital signs
title_ko: 활력 징후를 재서 적기
text_en: Measure vital signs every five minutes and record them for the first thirty minutes: blood pressure, pulse, breathing rate, temperature and blood oxygen saturation.
text_ko: 활력 징후를 오 분마다 재서 처음 삼십 분 동안 적는다. 재는 것은 혈압, 맥박, 호흡수, 체온, 혈중 산소 포화도다.

It reflects the equipment and practice of that time and is not the current procedure. Do not present these sentences as the agency's own words. Do not name or advise any medicine. Not a diagnosis.
numbers: Every 5 minutes on a 0-30 minute table (JSC-48522-E4, Chest Pain - Acute, step 3).

title_en: Watch the heart trace and listen to the chest
title_ko: 심전도를 지켜보고 가슴 소리 듣기
text_en: Monitor the heart's electrical trace. With a stethoscope, check whether the heart sounds are regular or irregular and whether the breath sounds are louder, quieter or absent, or include crackles or wheezes.
text_ko: 심전도를 지켜본다. 청진기로 심장 소리가 규칙적인지 불규칙한지, 숨소리가 커졌는지 작아졌는지 들리지 않는지, 거품 터지는 소리나 쌕쌕거리는 소리가 나는지 확인한다.

title_en: Contact the flight surgeon; what the checklist says when that fails
title_ko: 지상의 담당 의사에게 연락하기, 연락이 닿지 않을 때
text_en: Contact the flight surgeon. If the surgeon cannot be reached for several minutes or longer and the pain suggests a heart attack (pressure feeling, central or left-sided pain, pain spreading to the left arm or jaw, sweating), the checklist has treatment the crew starts on its own. It involves medicines and is not reproduced here.
text_ko: 지상의 담당 의사에게 연락한다. 몇 분이 넘도록 연락이 닿지 않고 통증이 심장 발작을 시사하면(누르는 듯한 느낌, 가운데나 왼쪽의 통증, 왼팔이나 턱으로 퍼지는 통증, 식은땀) 승무원이 먼저 시작하는 처치가 점검표에 따로 정해져 있다. 그 처치에는 약이 들어 있어 여기에는 옮기지 않았다.
